en: The Mahāyāna Vaipulya Buddhāvatamsaka Sūtra, Scroll One.
Translated by the Tripitaka Master of the Western Heaven, the Court Scattered Official and Acting Minister of the Court of State Ceremonial,
the Great Master of Fan (Sanskrit) and Imperially Invested Purple-Robed Śramaṇa, Subject Dharmapāla, and others, by imperial decree.
Thus have I heard:

At one time, the Blessed One was staying at Vulture Peak Mountain in the city of Rājagṛha, together with a great assembly of one thousand two hundred and fifty bhikṣus, all of whom were arhats whose outflows were exhausted.

Furthermore, there was a great assembly of bodhisattvas, headed by the Bodhisattva Maitreya and the Bodhisattva Mañjuśrī, together with countless other devas, nāgas, yakṣas, gandharvas, vidyādharas, ṛṣis, and celestial maidens.
At that time, the World-Honored One addressed the Venerable Mahākāśyapa, saying: “Kāśyapa!

Now, for the sake of bringing all roots of goodness to maturity in those bodhisattvas who have newly resolved their minds, I shall proclaim a teaching; listen attentively and apply your minds with great care!”
At that time, Mahākāśyapa addressed the Buddha, saying: “Excellent,
World-Honored One!”
"I shall receive the teaching and listen. The Buddha said, "Kāśyapa!"

To the east, passing from this buddha-field through as many worlds as there are grains of sand in one Ganges River, there is a world named Vyuṣṭavyūha. In that land there is a Buddha, titled Sthitahasta-paramaśrī Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha, who currently resides there, teaching and benefiting beings.

In that buddha-field, there is a bodhisattva mahāsattva named Virajagati, who shall succeed that buddha and attain the fruit of anuttarā-samyak-saṃbodhi, appearing in the world as the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha named Nityasamādhipāṇi-paramaśrī.

“Kāśyapa! If there are sons or daughters of good family who abide in the Bodhisattva vehicle and, upon hearing the name of this Tathāgata Supreme Auspiciousness of the Hand of Samādhi and the name of the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Free from Dust Steps, are able to recite, remember, and uphold them, such persons will, upon being reborn, attain the knowledge of past lives; for a hundred kalpas they shall turn their backs on birth and death, be able to gather immeasurable masses of merit, and draw near to the realization of the fruit of Anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi.”
"Furthermore, Kāśyapa!

To the east of this buddha-field, beyond worlds as numerous as the sands of two Gaṅgā rivers, there is a world named Great Bodhimaṇḍa-Adorned Sublime Love. In that land there is a Buddha, titled Lotus Supreme Auspiciousness Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha, who currently dwells there, teaching and benefiting beings."

In that buddha-field, there is a bodhisattva mahāsattva named Padmapāṇi, who shall succeed that buddha and attain the fruit of anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi, appearing in the world under the name of the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha Padmottararāja.
“Kāśyapa!

If there are sons of good family or daughters of good family abiding in the Bodhisattva vehicle who, upon hearing the name of the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha Padma-uttama-śrī and the name of the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Padmapāṇi, are able to recite, remember, and uphold them, such persons will, upon being reborn, attain the knowledge of past lives. They will always be born by lotus-transformation (*upapāduka*) and remain unstained by any worldly things, transcending all unwholesome dharmas just as a lotus is not defiled by water. They shall attain non-retrogression from *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*, turn their backs on birth and death for thirty thousand kalpas, gather immeasurable masses of merit, and draw near to the realization of the fruit of *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*.
"Furthermore, Kāśyapa!

To the east of this buddha-field, passing through worlds as numerous as the sands of three Gaṅgā rivers, there is a world named Virajagarbha. In that land there is a Buddha, titled Sūryamaṇḍalaprabhāsa-jayaśrī Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha, who currently dwells there, teaching and benefiting beings."

In that buddha-field, there is a bodhisattva mahāsattva named Sūryaprabha (Sunlight), who will succeed that buddha and attain the fruit of anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi, appearing in the world as the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha named Sarvāryaśrīparipūrṇottamasarvalakṣaṇālaṃkṛtakāya (The One Whose Body is Adorned with All Supreme Marks, Perfectly Complete with the Auspiciousness of All Nobles).

“Kāśyapa! If there are sons of good family or daughters of good family dwelling in the Bodhisattva vehicle who, upon hearing the name of the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha Most Victorious and Auspicious Radiance of the Solar Orb (Sūryamaṇḍalaprabhāsottamaśrī), as well as the name of the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Solar Radiance (Sūryaprabha), are able to recite, remember, and uphold them, such persons will, upon being reborn, attain the knowledge of past lives. Riding upon the illumination of the solar orb, they shall illuminate all wholesome dharmas; they will never again be born to fall into the three evil realms, nor will they experience doubt, confusion, or fear. They shall attain non-retrogression from Anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi, turn their backs on birth and death for a thousand kalpas, and draw near to the realization of the fruit of Anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi.”
"Furthermore, Kāśyapa!

To the east of this buddha-field, passing through worlds as numerous as the sands of four Gaṅgā rivers, there is a world named Vaśitāprāpta. In that land there is a Buddha, titled Ekaratnacchatrottama Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha, who currently resides there, teaching and benefiting beings."

“Kāśyapa! If there are sons of good family or daughters of good family dwelling in the Bodhisattva vehicle who, upon hearing the name of this One Jewel Parasol, Most Supreme Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha, are able to recite, remember, and uphold it, such persons, upon being reborn, will attain the knowledge of past lives (*pūrvajātismara*). They will not be born into inferior lineages, nor will they be born into impoverished lineages; wherever they are born, they will always be born into royal palaces. In their places of birth, they will encounter no obstacles regarding their mother, no obstacles regarding their father, no obstacles regarding wealth and status, and no obstacles regarding illness. They shall attain non-retrogression from *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*, turn their backs on birth and death for thirty thousand kalpas, and draw near to the realization of the fruit of *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*.”
"Furthermore, Kāśyapa!

To the east of this buddha-field, beyond worlds as numerous as the sands of five Ganges Rivers, there is a world named Viśuddhagarbha. In that land dwells a Buddha named Sthiratarottamaśrī Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha, who currently resides there, teaching and benefiting beings."
“Kāśyapa! When that Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha of Supreme Auspiciousness was formerly practicing the bodhisattva path, he made this great vow:

‘May it be that when I attain buddhahood in the future, if there are sons or daughters of good family dwelling in the bodhisattva vehicle who, upon hearing my name, are able to recite, remember, and uphold it, those persons shall always be able to leave the household life in every birth and lifetime; having left the household life, they shall all obtain one thousand samādhis, and within each samādhi, they shall further realize hundreds of thousands of koṭi-nayuta gates of samādhi, such that all the samādhis they have attained shall never be lost.’”
One shall be able to behold, pay homage to, and hear the Dharma from ten thousand Buddhas who have already entered parinirvāṇa in the past;

likewise, regarding all Buddhas seen and the Dharma heard throughout the present and future worlds, it shall be the same. One shall attain non-retrogression from *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*, and for a thousand kalpas in every successive birth, one shall turn one's back on saṃsāra and draw near to the realization of the fruit of *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*.

“Kāśyapa, if any sons of good family or daughters of good family who abide in the Bodhisattva vehicle hear the name of this Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha, Most Supreme Auspiciousness, and are able to recite, remember, and uphold it, such persons shall obtain all that they seek through those very modes of practice.”
"Furthermore, Kāśyapa!

To the east of this buddha-field, passing through worlds as numerous as the sands of six Gaṅgā rivers, there is a world named Ratnavyūha. In that land there is a Buddha, titled Ratnacakra-prabhāsa-abhyudgata-śrī-rāja Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha, who currently resides there, teaching and benefiting beings."

“Kāśyapa! If there are sons of good family or daughters of good family dwelling in the Bodhisattva vehicle who, upon hearing the name of the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha Ratnacakra-prabhāsa-abhyudgata-śrī-rāja, are able to recite, remember, and uphold it, those persons will, upon being reborn, attain the knowledge of past lives; they will possess mindfulness and wisdom with all marks perfected, shall achieve speech that inspires faith and compliance, and obtain uninterrupted eloquence in speech.”

Kāśyapa! This person, among all the eloquences in the world of devas and humans, shall not be intimidated, discouraged, or interrupted by others, and shall always possess uninterrupted eloquence in speech.

Furthermore, if any son or daughter of good family can recite the name of that Buddha, when such a person listens to the Dharma, they will behold the sacred marks of a Buddha appear before them. Regarding all dharmas previously unheard, as soon as they receive and study them, they will immediately attain boundless hundreds of thousands of millions of billions of *anuvartaka-dhāraṇīs*.

Moreover, within this Jambudvīpa, they will be able to know everything according to what sentient beings seek; thereafter, they will skillfully preach the Dharma in accordance with those beings' faith and understanding. They shall attain non-retrogression from *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*, turn their backs on birth and death for *asaṃkhyeya* hundreds of thousands of millions of billions of kalpas, and be able to gather immeasurable accumulations of merit.
The Mahāyāna Vaipulya Buddhābhiṣeka Sūtra, Scroll One.
The Mahāyāna Vaipulya Buddhābhiṣeka Sūtra, Scroll Two.
Translated by the Tripiṭaka Master from the Western Heaven, Chao San Dafu, Acting Minister of the Court of State Ceremonial, Chuánfàn.
The Great Master, the Purple-Robed Śramaṇa and Subject Fa-hu, and others, respectfully translated by imperial decree:

"Furthermore, Kāśyapa, thirty thousand worlds away from this buddha-field to the south, there is a world named Delightful Sound. In that land dwells a Buddha named Boundless Footprint Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha, who currently resides there, teaching and benefiting beings."

“Kāśyapa! If there are sons of good family or daughters of good family dwelling in the Bodhisattva vehicle who, upon hearing the name of that Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha Anantapadavikrama, are able to recite, remember, and uphold it, such persons will, upon being reborn, attain the knowledge of past lives (pūrvanivāsajñāna) and obtain the Bodhisattva samādhi called ‘Pure Lunar Disc’ (candramaṇḍalaviśuddha). Having dwelt in this samādhi, they will personally behold as many Buddhas, World-Honored Ones, as there are grains of sand in the Ganges River in the eastern direction.”

In this way, throughout the south, west, north, the four intermediate directions, and above and below—pervading the ten directions—they behold all the Buddhas, World-Honored Ones, as numerous as the sands of the Ganges in each and every direction; they listen to and receive the teachings from those respective Buddhas, World-Honored Ones, and are able to understand them all.

They constantly encounter the appearance of Buddhas in the world and never for a moment depart from the presence of the Buddhas, World-Honored Ones, until they reach the ultimate limit of realizing Bodhi, attaining non-retrogression from Anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi.
For thirty-five thousand kalpas, they turn their backs on birth and death, and are able to gather immeasurable masses of merit.

"Furthermore, Kāśyapa, thirty-five worlds away from this buddha-field to the south, there is a world named Most Excellent Fragrance. In that land dwells a Buddha, titled Boundless Fragrance Most Excellent King Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha, who currently resides there, teaching and benefiting beings."
“Kāśyapa! When that Tathāgata Anantagandharāja was formerly practicing the bodhisattva path, he made this great vow:

‘May it be that when I attain Buddhahood in the future, if there are sons of good family or daughters of good family dwelling in the Bodhisattva vehicle who, upon hearing my name, are able to recite, remember, and uphold it, these people shall obtain manifold merits, namely: in every place and in every birth they take, they shall attain the knowledge of past lives;’”
With the holy life perfected, my body shall be adorned with the thirty-two marks of a great man;
furthermore, all those in other buddha-fields who are touched by the light shall gather here, and for their sake, I shall bring all supreme practices for enlightenment to fulfillment.

Furthermore, if this great earth were filled everywhere with a great conflagration and set ablaze, and after it had burned, various kinds of precious jewels were to appear upon the earth and be distributed to all who came seeking them, yet that [earth] would not exhibit even the slightest sign of agitation;
such a person shall attain non-retrogression from *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*, turn their back on birth and death for thirty thousand *kalpas*, and be able to gather immeasurable masses of merit.
"Furthermore, Kāśyapa!

To the south, passing from this buddha-field through as many worlds as there are grains of sand in one Ganges River—[the name of this world is missing from the Sanskrit original]—there is a Buddha in that land named Ratnottama Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha, who currently resides there, teaching and benefiting beings."

“Kāśyapa! If there are sons of good family or daughters of good family dwelling in the Bodhisattva vehicle who, upon hearing the name of that Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha Ratnottama, are able to recite, remember, and uphold it, these persons will, upon being reborn, attain the knowledge of past lives. Furthermore, while still in the mother’s womb, they shall behold the Buddha, and that Buddha will encourage and praise them, saying:
‘Son of good family!’”
"You shall bring the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment (*anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*) to maturity; therefore, emerge quickly from your mother’s womb.
For a thousand kalpas, you have turned your back on birth and death, yet you have been able to gather and accumulate immeasurable masses of merit (*puṇya-skandha*).
"Furthermore, Kāśyapa!

To the west of this buddha-field, passing through as many worlds as there are grains of sand in three Ganges Rivers, there is a world named Aparijñāta (Unknown). In that land there is a Buddha, titled Mahāprabhāsa-pratibhāsa Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha, who currently resides there, teaching and benefiting beings."

“Kāśyapa! If there are sons or daughters of good family who abide in the Bodhisattva vehicle and, upon hearing the name of that Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha Great Radiant Illumination, are able to recite, remember, and uphold it, such persons will, upon being reborn, attain the knowledge of past lives and obtain the supreme samādhi of the Sun’s Radiance. Having abided in this samādhi, they shall behold as many Buddhas, World-Honored Ones, as there are grains of sand in the Ganges River; and just as the merits of great bodhisattvas such as Anabhibhū are praised, so too shall the merits of these persons be likewise extolled.”

“Kāśyapa! Furthermore, if a woman hears the name of that Tathāgata while in her mother’s womb, she will not again take on the female form in her subsequent birth; once this retribution has ended, she shall become a man.”
"Why is this? It is because by hearing the names of such Tathāgatas of great supernormal powers and great majesty, one is able to receive and uphold them.
At that time, the World-Honored One spoke in verse:
“If there is a woman dwelling in her mother’s womb who hears the supreme name of the Buddha,
the Great Sage, she shall transform this female body and become a wise man;
having realized unsurpassed, great Bodhi, she will benefit all classes of sentient beings.”
He is able to serve as a refuge for all sentient beings throughout the heavens and the human realm.

Furthermore, Kāśyapa, if there are sons or daughters of good family who abide in the Bodhisattva vehicle and, upon hearing the name of that Tathāgata, are able to recite, remember, and uphold it, such persons shall turn their backs on birth and death for incalculable *asaṃkhyeya* kalpas, gather immeasurable masses of merit, and draw near to the realization of the fruit of *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*.
"Furthermore, Kāśyapa!

To the north of this buddha-field, beyond forty thousand worlds, there is a world named Ratnavatī. In that land there is a Buddha, titled Ratnakuśeśayavairocanaśrī Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha, who currently dwells there, teaching and benefiting beings."

“Kāśyapa! If there are sons of good family or daughters of good family dwelling in the Bodhisattva vehicle who, upon hearing the name of that Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha Ratnakusumita-samantaprabhā-śrī, are able to recite, remember, and uphold it, these persons will, upon being reborn, attain the knowledge of past lives and obtain the *bodhisattva* samādhi called ‘Jewel Moon. Having dwelt in this samādhi, they will be able to understand the languages and sounds of all sentient beings, receive the empowerment of the Buddhas, and achieve unimpeded eloquence in speech.”
If there are sentient beings who wish to see him dwelling in mid-air proclaiming the various dharmas, this person can immediately manifest himself according to their wishes;
furthermore, within this Jambudvīpa, whatever sounds all sentient beings may desire to hear, this person is able to understand each and every one of them.

Furthermore, if all sentient beings in this trichiliocosm were to produce whatever sounds or utterances they desired or sought, this person would know them all and preach the Dharma to each according to their faith and understanding;
they shall attain non-retrogression from *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi* and turn their backs on birth and death for sixty thousand kalpas.
"Furthermore, Kāśyapa!

To the east of this buddha-field, beyond sixty thousand worlds, there is a world named Sarvaratna (All Jewels). In that land there is a Buddha, titled Ratnagarbha Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha, who currently resides there, teaching and benefiting beings."

“Kāśyapa! If there are sons of good family or daughters of good family who abide in the Bodhisattva vehicle and, upon hearing the name of that Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha Ratnagarbha, are able to recite, remember, and uphold it, these persons will, upon being reborn, attain the knowledge of past lives and shall achieve the realization of the seven factors of enlightenment.”

"Furthermore, Kāśyapa, to the east of this buddha-field, beyond worlds as numerous as the sands of the Ganges, there is a world named Ratnaprabhāsa. In that land there is a Buddha, titled Ratnaśrī Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha, who currently resides there, teaching the Dharma and transforming sentient beings."

“Kāśyapa! If there are sons or daughters of good family who abide in the Bodhisattva vehicle and, upon hearing the name of that Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha Ratnaśrī, are able to recite, remember, and uphold it, such persons will be able to generate a manifold mass of merit.”

“Kāśyapa! Suppose there were sons of good family or daughters of good family dwelling in the Bodhisattva vehicle who gathered vast quantities of precious jewels, their accumulation equal in measure to Sumeru, the King of Mountains, and performed such acts of giving, making extensive offerings to the Buddhas, the World-Honored Ones, continuing this practice of generosity for hundreds of thousands of millions of billions of years without interruption;

yet if another person, upon hearing the name of that Ratnasaṃbhava Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha, were able to recite, remember, and uphold it, the immeasurable merit of the former giving would not equal even one hundredth part of this merit, nor one thousandth part, nor one hundred-thousandth part, nor one asaṃkhyeya part; it would not equal even a calculable part, a figurative part, or any comparison whatsoever.”
At that time, the World-Honored One spoke these verses:
“In all the Buddha-fields of the east, And those in the south, west, and north— In every direction,
the World-Honored Ones currently dwelling Illumine sentient beings and bring them benefit.”
One should know whether it is the proper time or not; day and night, one should always give rise to thoughts of reverence.
With palms joined in devout respect, one should sincerely resolve to have faith and pay homage to the Supreme One, the Most Victorious among Men.
How can one know and clearly comprehend, and with intention and thought pay homage to the Honored One among Men—
namely, that throughout a thousand kalpas, it is extremely difficult to encounter the appearance of a Buddha in the world?
If you wish to pay homage to all Buddhas and seek unsurpassed bodhi,
having heard the names of the Buddhas spoken by the Buddha, you should constantly take refuge in them.
I now have no further desires; I seek only to give birth within the Buddha’s wisdom.
Whatever roots of goodness I may thereby attain, I dedicate them toward the inconceivable wisdom of the Buddha.
If a person wishes to make offerings to all Buddhas, they should constantly maintain the thought that the Buddhas are inconceivable;
having heard the names of those Buddhas, they should proclaim them extensively for the sake of others.
Desiring to cause millions of classes of sentient beings to transcend the two realms of existence and attain liberation,
once they have heard the names of those Buddhas, they shall uphold them and no longer be born in the human world.
Wishing to cause billions of Buddha-fields to tremble by means of a single toe,
and having heard the names of those Buddhas, one should uphold them and widely proclaim them for the sake of many people.
If one has previously made offerings to the various Buddhas, And upon hearing the Buddha’s name, is able to receive and uphold it,
Not merely for one, ten, or twenty lifetimes, But throughout many births, this constitutes planting the roots of goodness.
If one hears the names of the Buddhas and is able to uphold them, compared to the person who upholds the names of the Buddhas,
the merit from giving gold and jewels as numerous as the sands of the Ganges does not equal even a hundredth part.
Those who hear the names of the Buddhas and uphold them shall attain the marks of a supreme human body;
with wondrous form and dignified majesty, they shall dwell in the world, and upon leaving the household life, they will be worthy of receiving offerings from gods and humans.

When the Buddha had finished speaking this sutra, those bhikṣus, the great assembly of bodhisattva-mahāsattvas, the Venerable Mahākāśyapa, and all the world’s devas, humans, asuras, gandharvas, and others, having heard what the Buddha taught, were all greatly rejoiced; they believed, accepted, and practiced it accordingly.
The Mahāyāna Vaipulya Sūtra on the Buddha’s Crown, Spoken by the Buddha, Scroll II.
